nodes.description: The standard intervention for profound DFNB28. The lesion is in the hair bundle, and the implant stimulates the auditory nerve directly, so it works downstream of the failed stereocilia. Three Afghan siblings homozygous for an exon 7 nonsense allele reached aided thresholds of 23 to 30 dB HL one month after activation, and the two younger ones had open-set phoneme recognition of up to 77% at ten months. This is a single family and a short follow-up.

evidence.reference_title: A New Pathogenic Variant in the TRIOBP Associated with Profound Deafness Is Remediable with Cochlear Implantation.
evidence.snippet: One month after activation, the pure-tone averages with the CI processor were between 30 and 23 dBHL.

evidence.reference_title: A New Pathogenic Variant in the TRIOBP Associated with Profound Deafness Is Remediable with Cochlear Implantation.
evidence.snippet: Ten months after the first activation of the implant, open-set speech audiometry test could be performed for the first time in the 2 younger CI recipients (S5 and S9), and they could identify up to a maximum 77% phonemes correctly.

nodes.description: Without TRIOBP-4/5 the stereocilium itself develops but its rootlet does not. Mice lacking both isoforms form no rootlets; mice lacking only TRIOBP-5 form rootlets that are dysmorphic, thin in the cuticular plate but abnormally wide and long inside the stereocilium. The rootlet is also where TRIOBP-5 meets its partners: ANKRD24 forms a ring at the insertion point and keeps TRIOBP-5 in the lower rootlet, and the two depend on each other for localisation. Taperin (TPRN, DFNB79) works from the taper above and is needed to keep TRIOBP-5 and ANKRD24 in the rootlets of the mechanosensory rows, so DFNB28 and DFNB79 converge on the same structure.

evidence.reference_title: TRIOBP-5 sculpts stereocilia rootlets and stiffens supporting cells enabling hearing.
evidence.snippet: A loss of TRIOBP-5 in mouse results in dysmorphic rootlets that are abnormally thin in the cuticular plate but have increased widths and lengths within stereocilia cores, and causes progressive deafness recapitulating the human phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: ANKRD24 organizes TRIOBP to reinforce stereocilia insertion points.
evidence.snippet: TRIOBP-5 is mislocalized in Ankrd24KO/KO hair cells, and ANKRD24 no longer localizes with rootlets in mice lacking TRIOBP-5; exogenous DsRed-TRIOBP-5 restores endogenous ANKRD24 to rootlets in these mice.

evidence.snippet: Stereocilia that lack TPRN develop warped rootlets with gradual loss of TRIOBP-5 and ANKRD24 from mechanosensory rows starting postnatally.

nodes.description: Amplification is the usual first step for the moderate and moderate-to-severe presentations, where useful residual hearing remains. It raises the stimulus reaching a bundle that still partly works rather than bypassing the lesion.

TRIOBP-4 and TRIOBP-5 share an N-terminal region carrying two repeat motifs, R1 and R2, of which R1 is the principal actin-binding domain. Purified TRIOBP-4 packs actin filaments into bundles that are denser than those made by espin, the cross-linker of the stereocilium shaft, and that resemble the rootlet. In the hair cell, the upper rootlet inside the stereocilium is bundled mainly by TRIOBP-4, while the lower rootlet inside the cuticular plate is bundled by both TRIOBP-4 and TRIOBP-5. TRIOBP-5 thickens the rootlet to its mature dimensions. Truncating alleles remove this bundling activity from the hair cell and, for TRIOBP-5, from the supporting cells.

evidence.reference_title: Actin-bundling protein TRIOBP forms resilient rootlets of hair cell stereocilia essential for hearing.
evidence.snippet: In vitro, purified TRIOBP isoform 4 protein organizes actin filaments into uniquely dense bundles reminiscent of rootlets but distinct from bundles formed by espin, an actin crosslinker in stereocilia.

evidence.reference_title: R1 motif is the major actin-binding domain of TRIOBP-4.
evidence.snippet: These results indicate that R1 motif is the major actin-binding domain of TRIOBP-4, and the binding of R2 motif with actin filaments is nonspecific.

evidence.reference_title: TRIOBP-5 sculpts stereocilia rootlets and stiffens supporting cells enabling hearing.
evidence.snippet: Using 3 new Triobp mouse models, we report that TRIOBP-5 is essential for thickening bundles of F-actin in rootlets, establishing their mature dimensions and for stiffening supporting cells of the auditory sensory epithelium.

nodes.description: A milder presentation reported in a small number of families in which at least one allele truncates only TRIOBP-5: congenital moderate loss that was stable over 15 years in a Dutch patient, and peri- to postlingual moderate-to-severe loss in three Polish siblings. The Dutch authors note that the predicted effects of the alleles do not fully explain the milder phenotype, so this is recorded as the observed range rather than as a rule that TRIOBP-5-only alleles are mild.

nodes.description: The phenotype of the founding families: bilateral, symmetrical, prelingual, profound sensorineural loss, seen in Palestinian, Pakistani and Afghan families whose alleles truncate both TRIOBP-4 and TRIOBP-5. No conductive component was found, and vision was normal despite TRIOBP-4/5 expression in the retina.

evidence.snippet: Hearing loss in family K was sensorineural, bilateral, symmetrical, and profound; the mode of inheritance appeared to be recessive.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in a novel isoform of TRIOBP that encodes a filamentous-actin binding protein are responsible for DFNB28 recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss.
evidence.snippet: No signs of mixed hearing loss were noted, and vision was normal.

evidence.reference_title: A New Pathogenic Variant in the TRIOBP Associated with Profound Deafness Is Remediable with Cochlear Implantation.
evidence.snippet: Clinical audiometry demonstrated profound sensorineural hearing loss in all 3 affected siblings (2 males and 1 female), and they were implanted unilaterally.

nodes.description: TRIOBP-4 and TRIOBP-5 are also present in the actin bundles of Deiters' cells and pillar cells, the supporting cells that hold the outer hair cells in the reticular lamina. Without TRIOBP-5 the apical surface of these cells is softer, and atomic force mapping shows that TRIOBP deficiency disrupts the opposing stiffness gradients between rows of hair cells and supporting cells. The authors propose that this mechanical change contributes to hearing loss alongside the bundle lesion. The size of that contribution is not known, it has been measured only in early postnatal mouse cochleae, and nothing comparable exists for patients, so the edge into the hearing phenotype is recorded with unknown intermediates.
nodes.id: Reduced Apical Stiffness of Organ of Corti Supporting Cells

evidence.reference_title: TRIOBP-5 sculpts stereocilia rootlets and stiffens supporting cells enabling hearing.
evidence.snippet: Using PFT-AFM, we observed that the absence of TRIOBP-5 in the organ of Corti resulted in a significant decrease in the local axial stiffness of the supporting cells within the reticular lamina.

evidence.reference_title: Unbalanced bidirectional radial stiffness gradients within the organ of Corti promoted by TRIOBP.
evidence.snippet: Deafness-associated TRIOBP deficiencies significantly disrupted the magnitude and orientation of these bidirectional radial stiffness gradients.

nodes.description: The rootlet is what makes a stereocilium stiff at its pivot and able to survive large deflections. Without it, inner hair cell bundles are roughly twice as compliant to fluid-jet stimulation, and a single large deflection often lowers their stiffness further, a sign of damage. Mechanotransduction responses are present, so the transducer is not the primary lesion; the authors' reading is that the bundle is mechanically unsuited to normal sensitivity and is easily damaged.

evidence.reference_title: Actin-bundling protein TRIOBP forms resilient rootlets of hair cell stereocilia essential for hearing.
evidence.snippet: We found that TriobpΔex8/Δex8 stereocilia are about twice more flexible as compared to TriobpΔex8/+ stereocilia, when deflected by fluid-jet stimuli of progressively increasing intensity.

evidence.reference_title: Actin-bundling protein TRIOBP forms resilient rootlets of hair cell stereocilia essential for hearing.
evidence.snippet: Taken together, our data suggests that even though the MET machinery is operational in TriobpΔex8/Δex8 hair cells, these cells are unlikely to have normal mechanosensitivity in vivo due to both the decreased pivotal stiffness and increased fragility of the stereocilia bundle.

nodes.description: Bundles that develop without rootlets then fuse and degenerate. In mice lacking TRIOBP-4/5 this is widespread by postnatal day 16, around the onset of hearing. When only TRIOBP-5 is lost the course is slower: stereocilia, mainly of the tallest outer hair cell row, are lost by about postnatal day 40, plausibly by detachment at fragile pivot points. The slower course in TRIOBP-5-only mice parallels the milder human phenotype reported with TRIOBP-5-only alleles, but no human temporal bone or bundle morphology has been described.

evidence.reference_title: Whole exome sequencing identifies TRIOBP pathogenic variants as a cause of post-lingual bilateral moderate-to-severe sensorineural hearing loss.
evidence.snippet: The pathogenic variant p.Gln268Leufs*610 disrupts the TRIOBP-4 and TRIOBP-5 isoforms (both expressed exclusively in the inner ear and retina) whereas the second pathogenic variant c.514G>T, p.Gly1672* affects only TRIOBP-5.

nodes.description: Biallelic truncating TRIOBP alleles that remove the TRIOBP-4 and/or TRIOBP-5 isoforms. The founding alleles were nonsense and frameshift changes in the large exon shared by TRIOBP-4 and TRIOBP-5 (exon 6 in the human numbering used by the discovery papers), and later families add truncations further 3', in sequence unique to TRIOBP-5. No reported allele disrupts the ubiquitous TRIOBP-1 isoform, whose loss is embryonic lethal in mice; that is the most likely reason the mutational spectrum is confined to the exons upstream of the TRIOBP-1 promoter. Most alleles are truncating; missense changes reported in trans with a truncation (G1019R, R1221W) remain of uncertain significance.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in TRIOBP, which encodes a putative cytoskeletal-organizing protein, are associated with nonsyndromic recessive deafness.
evidence.snippet: These alleles include four nonsense (Q297X, R788X, R1068X, and R1117X) and two frameshift (D1069fsX1082 and R1078fsX1083) mutations, all located in exon 6 of TRIOBP.

evidence.reference_title: Actin-bundling protein TRIOBP forms resilient rootlets of hair cell stereocilia essential for hearing.
evidence.snippet: To date, all of the mutations of TRIOBP causing human deafness DFNB28 are located in exon 6 (Figure 1B), and only affect TRIOBP-4 and TRIOBP-5 (TRIOBP-4/5).

evidence.reference_title: Actin-bundling protein TRIOBP forms resilient rootlets of hair cell stereocilia essential for hearing.
evidence.snippet: Thus, TRIOBP-4 and/or TRIOBP-5 are essential for hearing whilst ubiquitously expressed TRIOBP-1 has an additional, essential role during development.

evidence.reference_title: Broadening the phenotype of DFNB28: Mutations in TRIOBP are associated with moderate, stable hereditary hearing impairment.
evidence.snippet: To our knowledge, p.Gly1672* is the first pathogenic variant identified in DFNB28 that does not affect isoform class TRIOBP-4.

evidence.reference_title: Elucidation of repeat motifs R1- and R2-related TRIOBP variants in autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss DFNB28 among indigenous South African individuals.
evidence.snippet: Family TS005 carrying variants c.572delC, p.Pro191Argfs*50, and c.3510_3513dupTGCA, p.Pro1172Cysfs*13, demonstrated perfect cosegregation with the deafness phenotype.

nodes.description: Ablates TRIOBP-4 and TRIOBP-5 while keeping TRIOBP-1, the same isoform pattern as the founding human alleles. Homozygotes are profoundly deaf; stereocilia develop without rootlets, are more compliant and fragile, and fuse and degenerate by postnatal day 16.

Removes TRIOBP-5 alone. Rootlets form but are dysmorphic, supporting cells are softer, and hearing declines from residual at four weeks to severe-to-profound by eight weeks. It is the model for the human alleles that truncate TRIOBP-5 only.
